newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs close up after mid-session correction.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs close up after mid-session correction.

text.p: Shares ended Monday's trading in positive territory despite a mid-afternoon consolidation that ate away at morning gains, brokers said.
The composite stock index closed 1.48 points higher at a provisional 842.28 after reaching a high of 849.12. Advancers beat decliners 587 to 337 as 56 million shares changed hands.
"The market was very, very encouraging today and the breadth of the buying was good," said Richard Kim of KLB Securities.
Banks were in the spotlight on the possibility of mergers and acquisitions and restructuring after South Korea's entry into the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development.
South Korea was invited to join the Paris-based club of rich nations on Friday.
SEOULBANK rose 300 won to its upper limit of 5,410. Its shares are at their lowest levels in almost 10 years. Dongnam Bank gained 310 won to 5,550, and Hanil Bank was up 100 won to 8,000.

Preferred shares were also actively sought after because they are considered to be undervalued compared to common shares. Daishin Securities preferred shares rose 300 won to 6,700. Tong Yang Cement preferred gained 510 won to its upper limit of 9,010. Anam Industrial preferred rose 450 won to 7,950.
Anam common shares ended up 500 won to 15,500 after resuming trading in the afternoon. The bourse halted trading in the morning after Anam announced a 15-for-100 bonus issue.
The December futures contract closed down 0.30 of a point to 88.40, while the KOSPI 200 index fell 0.10 of a point to 88.09.
Brokers said a short-term correction was possible Tuesday. But the rising trend was still on track, bolstered by hopes for an interest rate cut.
Customer deposits at brokerages have been steadily rising, and were at 2.7 trillion won, compared to 2.71 trillion won in margin loans held. -- KATHERINE BRUCE (822) 727 5644
